examples: 'entries' vs 'tools' vs 'scripts' vs 'sources' vs 'sops' vs 'sessions' vs 'methods' vs 'picks' as the array key in index.json files
'entry_count' vs 'source_count' vs 'sop_count' vs 'session_count' vs 'total_picks' as the count field
'team' vs 'added_by_team' vs 'populated_by' for recording which team created an entry
'version' vs 'schema' at top level of index files
'last_updated' vs 'generated' for timestamp field
'path' vs 'filename' vs 'file' for file references in entries
CROSS_REFERENCES.md vs cross-references.json for the same concept
thinktank_ vs think-tank- for think tank naming in teams/
naming_inconsistencies.recommendation: Standardize index schema: use 'items' or type-specific plural as array key, 'count' as count field, 'team' for attribution, 'version' for schema version, 'last_updated' for timestamps, 'file' for file references.

conventions_used.snake_case: Dominant for .py files and Go tool directories
conventions_used.kebab-case: Dominant for .md files, .json data files, and top-level directories
conventions_used.UPPER_CASE: Used for root documentation and TEMPLATE files
conventions_used.PREFIX-NNNN: Used for sequenced entries (KB, TEAM, SRC, SCR, TOOL, SOP, DG, PICK)

worst_inconsistencies: storage/scripts/ mixes kebab-case and snake_case filenames freely (33 files, ~50/50 split)
Every index.json has a different schema - no shared structure for array key, count field, or attribution
SOP filenames don't match SOP IDs for entries 026-028
storage/coordination/teams/ files use at least 3 naming conventions simultaneously
CROSS_REFERENCES.md (UPPER_SNAKE) vs cross-references.json (kebab) for same concept in same directory
Duplicate data: KB-0012/KB-0013 identical titles, SRC-0018/SRC-0039 same API, REGISTRY.json duplicates KB tag_index
recommendations_priority: P0: Standardize index.json schema across all resource types (unified field names)
P1: Enforce naming convention per file type (.py=snake, .md=kebab, .json=kebab, dirs=kebab)
P2: Standardize ID prefixes to 4-digit zero-padded
P2: Clean up empty team directories
